title: Epochal holdout + priority sampling for per-domain calibration packs
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: We need a reproducible curation and sampling strategy to build per-domain calibration packs used for FP8 and INT8 quantization profile validation. Existing packs are heavily traffic-weighted and occasionally over-represent recent spikes. This ticket defines an 'epochal holdout + priority sampling' approach: we split historical production prompt traffic into discrete epochs, hold out a final epoch for validation, and sample training/ calibration sets by combining stratified domain quotas with priority weights for recent high-signal exemplars. Goals: 1) ensure per-domain coverage across intent families and context-length slices; 2) avoid leakage between calibration and validation epochs; 3) prioritize stable high-frequency exemplars while preserving long-tail diversity required to catch precision regressions post-quantization. Outcome: a documented, automated pack generator and a CI gating job that produces per-domain packs and runs FP8/INT8 calibration + accuracy validation on PRs that affect quant kernels.
sampling_algorithm_summary: 1) Partition: bucket production prompts by domain label and by epoch (7-day rolling epochs by default). 2) Holdout: reserve the final epoch entirely as validation; no example from that epoch may appear in calibration packs. 3) Quotas: for each domain, compute target pack size N_domain = base + alpha * active_users(domain). 4) Slicing: within each domain, further slice by context-length quartiles, intent cluster (from existing clustering pipeline), and presence of external entities. 5) Priority weights: assign per-example weight = w_recency * w_freq * w_quality where w_recency decays by epoch distance, w_freq = log(1 + occurrences), w_quality derived from signal (non-NA evals, low-error rate). 6) Sampling: draw examples using weighted reservoir sampling with deduplication and per-slice minimums. 7) Exemplar anchoring: ensure top-k high-weight exemplars per domain are always included. 8) Synthetic augmentation: if a slice has fewer than min_examples, apply paraphrase augmentation (controlled, short paraphrases) up to 20% of a domain pack. 9) Output: a gzipped JSONL pack with provenance headers and deterministic seed metadata.
validation_and_metrics:
- Primary metrics: token-level perplexity shift (quantized vs fp baseline), top-1 answer-match rate for classification intents, and BLEU/ROUGE for text transforms where applicable.
- Stability checks: run 5 seeds for each quant profile (FP8, INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric) and report median and max deviation.
- Sensitivity: per-domain 'regression rate' = fraction of prompts with >delta threshold metric degradation.
- Acceptance thresholds: median perplexity increase < 3% and domain regression rate < 2% for non-critical domains; critical domains (billing, auth) require <1% regression.
- Automated checks: pack-level checksum, epoch isolation verification, duplication rate <0.5%.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pack generator produces per-domain packs for all active domains and stores them in s3://redwood-quant-calibration/packs/YYYY-MM-DD/
Holdout validation epoch is strictly isolated (no example overlap) verified by CI job
Calibration runs for FP8 and INT8 execute in CI and produce metrics dashboard link in PR comments
Quant regression gating flags PR if any critical domain exceeds regression thresholds
Documentation: sampling algorithm, parameter knobs, and provenance fields added to internal Confluence page with example outputs

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-prioritizing recency may miss long-tail regressions. Mitigation: enforce a minimum long-tail quota per domain (10%) and run monthly deep-tail scans.
Risk: noisy labels or bad domain tags. Mitigation: add a label confidence filter and fall back to 'unknown' domain grouping for manual triage.
Risk: synthetic augmentation introducing distributional shift. Mitigation: cap synthetic to 20% and restrict paraphrase transformations to length-preserving variants.
Risk: heavy compute cost in CI. Mitigation: run quant calibration on sampled subsets for PRs and full-pack nightly runs for release candidates.
